noteBlocks.md:
**Genome** — all of the genetic material of an organism. The whole set.
**Chromosome** — one long thread of DNA in the nucleus. A human body cell holds 46 of them.
**Gene** — a short length of DNA on a chromosome that controls one characteristic.
**Allele** — a different form of the same gene.

noteBlocks.prompt: A short length of DNA on a chromosome that controls one characteristic is called a ____.
noteBlocks.explain: A gene. The whole set of genetic material is the genome; a gene is one instruction inside it.

noteBlocks.prompt: How many pairs can you count, and what is different about the pair at the bottom right?

noteBlocks.md:
In the nucleus of a body cell the chromosomes sit in **functional pairs**: 23 pairs, so 46 chromosomes altogether. One of each pair came from the mother and one from the father.

Two kinds of cell break that rule. A **gamete** — a sperm cell or an ovum — carries only **one** of each pair, so 23 chromosomes. A **bacterium** has no nucleus at all, so its chromosomes are not in pairs either.

noteBlocks.prompt: A human body cell holds its chromosomes in 23 functional pairs. How many chromosomes is that altogether?
noteBlocks.explain: 23 pairs, two chromosomes in each pair, so 23 × 2 = 46.

noteBlocks.alt: A length of DNA drawn as a flat ladder. Each upright is a chain of phosphate circles and sugar pentagons; each rung is a pair of bases, A opposite T and C opposite G. A small twisted version beside it shows the same molecule as a double helix.
noteBlocks.caption: Two uprights, rungs between them, and a twist. That is the whole molecule.

noteBlocks.md:
Unwind one chromosome far enough and you reach **DNA**. Drawn flat, it is a ladder.

The two uprights are the **backbone**, built from a **phosphate** and a **sugar (deoxyribose)**, over and over.

The rungs are the **bases**, and they interlink across the middle in only two ways: **A with T**, and **C with G**. Those are the base-pairing rules.

Let the ladder twist and you have the **double helix**.

noteBlocks.prompt: In a DNA molecule, which base always pairs with C?
noteBlocks.explain: G. The two pairs are A with T and C with G, and nothing else is possible.

noteBlocks.title: Worked example: 28% of the bases in a length of DNA are A. Calculate the percentage that are C. [3]
noteBlocks.md:
**Step 1 — use the pairing rule.** A only pairs with T, so there must be just as many T bases: **28%**. **[1]**
**Step 2 — take that pair off 100.** 28 + 28 = 56, and 100 − 56 = **44%** left for C and G together. **[1]**
**Step 3 — share what is left.** C pairs with G, so those two are equal: 44 ÷ 2 = **22%**. **[1]**

Check it: 28 + 28 + 22 + 22 = 100.

noteBlocks.title: Show the halving
noteBlocks.md: Only quite a few got this right in Summer 2025. Write the pair total, the subtraction and the halving on separate lines: each step can earn a mark.

noteBlocks.prompt: In a different length of DNA, 31% of the bases are G. What percentage of the bases are A?
noteBlocks.explain: G pairs with C, so C is 31% too. That is 62% used, leaving 38% to share between A and T: 19% each.

noteBlocks.md:
A **gene** is a place on a chromosome and the characteristic it controls. An **allele** is one of the versions that can sit in that place. Flower colour is the gene; the version for red and the version for white are two of its alleles.

The other pair worth separating: a **chromosome** is a structure in the nucleus, while **DNA** is the molecule it is made of. A chromosome is made of DNA in the way a book is made of paper.

noteBlocks.prompt: Two pea plants carry the same gene for flower colour, but one holds the version for violet and the other the version for white. What word describes those two versions?
noteBlocks.explain: Alleles: different forms of the same gene. They sit at the same place on a pair of chromosomes.

noteBlocks.md:
**Higher tier.** The order of the bases is the code. Read it **three at a time**: each group of three — a **base triplet** — codes for one **amino acid**. Join the amino acids in that order and you have a protein.

So a length carrying 24 bases codes for 24 ÷ 3 = 8 amino acids.

steps.working: A pairs with T, so T is 28% too. 28 + 28 = 56%.
steps.decision: Start from the pairing rule, because it is the only fact the question gives you. Every A has a T opposite it, so those two percentages must match.
All four bases together are 100%, so whatever the first pair does not use is what the other pair has.

steps.working: Work along one base at a time: A → T, T → A, G → C …

steps.working: The pairing strand reads T A C G G T.

In one length of DNA, 36% of the bases are T.
Calculate the percentage of the bases that are C.
Show your working out.

scheme.for: A is the same as T: 36 + 36 = 72

hints: T only pairs with A, so there is the same percentage of each.
What is left over is shared equally between the other two bases.
parts.workedSolution: T pairs with A, so A is 36% as well: 36 + 36 = 72%. That leaves 100 − 72 = 28% for C and G together, and they are equal, so C is 28 ÷ 2 = 14%.

commonErrors.feedback: That is what is left for C and G together. They pair with each other, so they share it equally: halve it.
That takes 36% off 100 once. There are four bases, and A takes another 36% before anything is left for C and G.
The four bases are not present in equal amounts. Only T and A match each other; C and G share what is left.
The halving comes at the end, and it is what is LEFT that gets halved, not the percentage you were given.

parts.stem:
Each strand of DNA has a backbone built from two substances.
Name both of them.

accepted: a phosphate and a sugar called deoxyribose

hints: They alternate along each upright of the ladder.
parts.workedSolution: Phosphate and sugar (deoxyribose).

parts.stem: Describe the shape that the two strands of a DNA molecule form.
hints: The bases hold the two strands together while they twist.
parts.workedSolution: They form a double helix.

parts.stem:
In this length of DNA, 19% of the bases are C.
Calculate the percentage of the bases that are A.
Show your working out.

scheme.for: G is 19% as well, so the pair is 38%

hints: C pairs with G, so those two percentages match.
parts.workedSolution: C pairs with G, so G is also 19%: together 38%. What is left is 100 − 38 = 62%, shared equally between A and T, so A is 31%.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the share left for A and T together, and it still has to be halved between them.
Subtracting once treats DNA as though it had two bases. Take the pair off first, then halve what is left.

parts.stem:
One strand of this length of DNA carries 24 bases.
How many amino acids does it code for?
hints: Three bases make one amino acid, so divide.
parts.workedSolution: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 amino acids.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the number of bases. Three of them code for one amino acid, so there are fewer amino acids than bases.
Multiplying by three goes the wrong way. Each amino acid uses up three bases, so the count of amino acids is smaller.

parts.stem:
Describe the structure of a DNA molecule, and explain what is meant by the genome, a chromosome, a gene and an allele.
This question also assesses the quality of your written communication, including your use of specialist scientific terms.

bands.descriptor: Five or six of the indicative points, described in detail, with specialist terms used widely and accurately; the ideas are ordered very clearly and follow on from one another; spelling, punctuation and grammar make the meaning clear throughout.

Three or four of the indicative points; some specialist vocabulary; the ideas are ordered reasonably well and mostly follow on; spelling, punctuation and grammar are competent enough for the meaning to be clear.
One or two of the indicative points; little specialist vocabulary; the organisation may lack clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar may leave the intended meaning unclear.

indicativeContent.point: the genome is all of the genetic material of an organism
a chromosome is a long thread of DNA in the nucleus, and in a body cell they lie in functional pairs (23 pairs)
a gene is a short length of DNA on a chromosome that controls a characteristic
an allele is a different form of the same gene
the backbone of DNA is made of a phosphate and a sugar, deoxyribose
the bases interlink across the middle, A with T and C with G
the two strands twist round each other to form a double helix

scheme.for: banded: count the indicative points present, then place within the band on the quality of written communication — Band A [5]-[6] five or six points, Band B [3]-[4] three or four, Band C [1]-[2] one or two, [0] response not worthy of credit
scheme.examinerNote: Two losses to watch for. The first is a gene and an allele given the same definition, which costs a whole indicative point however well the rest is written. The second is the shape: only the words double helix earn that point, and 'spiral' or 'twisted ladder' does not. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Go outward from the smallest thing: bases, DNA, gene, chromosome, genome.
Give an example of an allele so that the difference from a gene is visible.
parts.workedSolution: A DNA molecule is built from two long strands. Each strand has a backbone made of a phosphate and a sugar, deoxyribose, repeating along its length, and the bases stick out from that backbone. The bases interlink across the middle in a fixed way: A always pairs with T, and C always pairs with G. The two strands twist around each other to form a double helix. A chromosome is one long thread of this DNA, held in the nucleus, and in a human body cell the chromosomes lie in functional pairs, 23 pairs in all. A gene is a short length of DNA on a chromosome that controls a characteristic, such as flower colour. An allele is a different form of the same gene, such as the allele for violet flowers and the allele for white flowers. Taken together, all of the genetic material of the organism is its genome.

commonErrors.feedback: A gene and an allele have been given the same definition. The gene is the place and the job; the allele is the version sitting there.

findTheMistake.stem:
Ciara is asked: 'In a length of DNA, 28% of the bases are A. Calculate the percentage of the bases that are C. [3]'
Her working:
studentWorking: A pairs with T, so T is 28% as well
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Lines 1 and 2 are exactly right, and they carry two of the three marks. Line 3 hands the whole of the remaining 44% to C. But C pairs with G, so those two must be equal and the 44% is shared between them.
correction: A pairs with T, so T is 28% as well
findTheMistake.feedback: Two marks of the three. A quick check catches the rest: add her four percentages up and you get 144, not 100.

prompts.prompt: What is the genome of an organism?
prompts.answer: The genome is all of the genetic material of an organism.

prompts.prompt: Define a gene, and then define an allele.
prompts.answer: A gene is a short length of DNA on a chromosome that controls a characteristic. An allele is a different form of the same gene.
keyWords: different form of the same gene

prompts.prompt: A human body cell holds ___ chromosomes, in ___ functional pairs. A gamete holds ___.
prompts.answer: A human body cell holds 46 chromosomes, in 23 functional pairs. A gamete holds 23.

prompts.prompt: Which two kinds of cell do NOT hold their chromosomes in functional pairs?
prompts.answer: Gametes, which carry one of each pair, and bacteria, which have no nucleus.

prompts.prompt: Describe the structure of DNA in one sentence.
prompts.answer: A phosphate and sugar (deoxyribose) backbone with interlinking bases, twisted into a double helix.
A pairs with T, and C pairs with G.

prompts.prompt: In a length of DNA, 20% of the bases are A. What percentage are G?
prompts.answer: 30%. A pairs with T, so T is 20% as well, which is 40% used. That leaves 60% for C and G together, and they are equal, so G is 30%.

prompts.prompt: Higher tier: how do you turn a number of bases into a number of amino acids?
prompts.answer: Divide by three, because a base triplet of three bases codes for one amino acid.
